reading: Each red straight segment gets a colour-8 diamond around it: the segment is the diamond's long diagonal, and at segment position i the diamond reaches min(i, L-1-i) cells out on both sides.

slots.subject: each red segment (segments row)
slots.shape: rhombus with the segment as its diagonal; half-width at position i = min(i, L-1-i)
slots.rest: the segment and all other cells stay

why: every non-segment 8 cell is within the rhombus spanned by one segment; segments are unchanged

reading: The 5x5 X pattern is squeezed into 3x3: the 4 corners go to the 3x3 corners, the centre stays the centre, and the 4 inner diagonal cells fill the 4 edge-middle cells (main-diagonal pair top and bottom, anti-diagonal pair left and right).

slots.subject: the 9 non-background cells of the X

why: the output holds exactly the 9 X cells, packed with no background
invariants: colour multiset of the non-background cells

reading: When two special-coloured cells (not 0 or 1) of the same colour lie 6 apart on one row or column (in outer blocks at the same local position), the cell exactly midway (the same spot in the middle block) takes that colour.

new_rows.name: mid
new_rows.datalog:
mid(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X1, C), cell(Y, X2, C), C > 1, X2 = X1 + 6, X = X1 + 3.
mid(Y, X) :- cell(Y1, X, C), cell(Y2, X, C), C > 1, Y2 = Y1 + 6, Y = Y1 + 3.

why: every changed cell is the midpoint of a same-colour special pair and takes that pair's colour; nothing else changes

reading: The output is the input tiled n times across and n times down, where n is the input's side length; every block is a full copy.
why: every block of the output equals the input; the block grid has the input's dimensions
invariants: the unit is the whole input, unchanged

reading: One large shape is cut off by the grid border and is a 2x scaled-up copy of one of the small shapes; the output is that matching small shape's bounding box.

slots.probe: the large object touching the border (partially visible, scaled x2)
slots.match: the candidate whose x2 scaling, clipped at the border, equals the probe's shape
slots.output: the matching candidate's box cut from the input

why: the output equals the box of the one small object whose scaled form agrees with the visible part of the border-cut object
invariants: the chosen object's shape and colours

reading: The grid is three 4x4 panels separated by colour-2 columns; they are overlaid into one 4x4 with priority 4 over 9 over 1 over 0.

slots.parts: the 3 panels cut by the 2 separator columns
slots.combine: per cell, the highest-priority colour present

why: each output cell is the highest-priority colour among the three panels at that position

reading: An 8x8 square has a full top-left 4x4 quadrant in two colours; the other three quadrants are its mirrors (left-right for top-right, up-down for bottom-left, 180 rotation for bottom-right), each recoloured by the hint cells already in that quadrant (a colour with no hint becomes 0).

slots.copies: horizontal mirror -> TR, vertical mirror -> BL, both -> BR
slots.key: per quadrant, each source colour maps to the hint colour seen at a matching position in that quadrant, or 0 if none

why: each quadrant's shape pattern is the mirrored source pattern; its colours agree with the hint cells there

reading: All-empty columns are deleted, then the objects (left to right) are shifted up or down so each one starts on the row where the previous one's path ends, forming one connected chain.

slots.subjects: the objects, ordered left to right
slots.move: vertical shift so the object's leftmost cell is on the row of the previous object's right end

why: the output width is the input width minus empty columns, and each object's shape is kept with only a vertical shift

reading: Every coloured cell extends a line of its own colour straight down to the bottom border.
why: below each coloured cell, every cell down to the bottom border has that cell's colour
invariants: cells above and beside the lines

reading: From the single 8 cell, a colour-5 staircase runs up-right and down-left to the borders: step 1 cell vertically, then a 3-cell horizontal run, repeated (going up: up then right; going down: down then left).

slots.step: one vertical cell then a horizontal run of 3 sharing its corner, repeated

why: the 5 cells form exactly the two staircases from the marker, clipped at the border; the marker stays
